recommendation: Keep the no-change audit commit. No FHIR core edit is recommended for FHIR-12393; future physical-manufacturer representation concerns should follow the later manufacturer-extension work rather than changing Medication.marketingAuthorizationHolder for this issue.
issue_request: FHIR-12393 was a Published/Not Persuasive with Modification FHIR-core Medication issue from DSTU2 asking Pharmacy to clarify Medication.manufacturer. The accepted resolution said the element meant the manufacturer of the medication, not the distributor, and that both description and definition needed clearer wording.
initial_application: The Jira comments record that Melva Peters added clarification that manufacturer was not intended to represent the distributor and link commit b0500f8b520d72851aba346483f21d1ded9a86b3. That commit subject appears to typo the tracker number as TR 12392, but the patch changed the Medication manufacturer definition to state that it was not intended to represent the distributor, matching FHIR-12393.
additional_context: Medication is active in source/fhir.ini, but the active current Medication source no longer has Medication.manufacturer. Later Pharmacy decisions FHIR-27030, FHIR-32759, and FHIR-35858 renamed manufacturer to sponsor, then to Medication.marketingAuthorizationHolder, and then corrected the MAH definition away from manufacturer-centered wording. Current fhir.ini maps old Medication.manufacturer to Medication.marketingAuthorizationHolder for version conversion, and current source plus search parameters use marketingAuthorizationHolder.
reconciliation: No source change was made. Adding the old not-distributor clarification to the current MAH element would conflict with later approved Pharmacy decisions rather than complete this DSTU2 clarification.
